verses.1: After two years, Pharaoh dreamed that he stood on a mountain.
verses.2: And behold, from the sky came seven beautiful birds of great beauty. They were healthy and strong.
verses.3: And behold, seven other cows were also standing behind them, from the dark sky. They were thin and skinny. They stood beside the other cows, on top of the hill.
verses.4: And we ate those ugly, withered grains of wheat. But there were also seven grains of wheat that were beautiful and healthy. Pharaoh was pleased with them.
verses.5: And he lay down and slept again. Then, he saw that seven lambs were standing in one place, in health and prosperity.
verses.6: And behold, seven slender branches and tendrils began to grow behind them.
verses.7: And the sharp thorns swallowed up all seven healthy and nutritious plants. Pharaoh became angry, and then he fell ill.
verses.8: In the morning, his spirit became terrified. He sent out all the magicians of Egypt and all their wise men. Pharaoh told them his plans, but there was no way to escape from those plans.
verses.9: And the secretary of the priests said to Pharaoh, “I will mention my sins today.”
verses.10: Pharaoh became angry with his servants. He put me in charge of the house of the priests and the officials.
verses.11: And one night, I and he dreamed together. He was a man with a mysterious appearance. We dreamed together.
verses.12: And there we had a Hebrew young man who was a servant of the priests. He was assigned to work for them. He solved our problems for us. He helped us out of difficult situations.
verses.13: And when he had freed us from this situation, then he placed me back on my feet. And he hung him there.
verses.14: And Pharaoh sent for Josue. He called him out of the tent, had him stand up, and ordered him to take off his clothes. Then he brought him before Pharaoh.
verses.15: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have a dream. But I cannot interpret it. I heard you say, ‘Listen to the dream and try to interpret it.’”
verses.16: And Joseph said to Pharaoh, “Without God, I cannot answer Pharaoh’s request.”
verses.17: And Pharaoh spoke to Joseph in a dream: “I am standing on the bank of the Nile.”
verses.18: And behold, from the east came seven flocks of sheep, all healthy and sound. They were white and pure.
verses.19: And behold, seven other gates stood behind them; they were filled with doors and passages. There were also many holes in the ground. I had never seen anything like this before in all of Egypt’s lands.
verses.20: And we ate the rotten and bad fruits, along with those seven healthy fruits from before.
verses.21: And they came to Kirbenah. But they didn’t know that they had arrived at Kirbenah. Their appearance was terrible, just as it was at the beginning.
verses.22: And in my dream, I saw that seven slaves were riding on one cart, filled with goods and treasures.
verses.23: And behold, seven lilies stood there, with their petals very thin and delicate. They were just beginning to bloom.
verses.24: And the sharp thorns swallowed up those seven good thorns. And he said to the hartumim, “There’s no one who can tell me.”
verses.25: And Joseph said to Pharaoh, “I dream that there is a king who is created by God. Tell Pharaoh about this.”
verses.26: Seven good things, seven years have passed since then. And seven good days have also passed since then. It’s just one dream after all.
verses.27: And the seven ripe fruits and the seven bad fruits will follow each other. It will be seven years of such conditions. And the seven rotten fruits will also be seven years of suffering.
verses.28: It is the thing that I said to Pharaoh. It was the work of God that made Pharaoh see it.
verses.29: Now, seven years have passed since that great disaster occurred throughout all of Egypt.
verses.30: And seven years of famine followed after them. They forgot about the whole year of famine in Egypt. And the famine destroyed the entire land.
verses.31: And the seventy will not know when they will die on this earth due to that famine. After all, it’s better to die in such a way.
verses.32: And in those times of great trouble, Pharaoh was warned several times, as the words from God were fulfilled. And God quickly acted upon these warnings.
verses.33: And now, Pharaoh will see a man who is wise and intelligent. He will put him in charge of the land of Egypt.
verses.34: The Pharaoh will do this, and he will carry out his plans on the land. He will settle the land of Egypt in seven years.
verses.35: And they shall store up all the good crops that have been grown this year, and they shall keep them under Pharaoh’s control. They will be used as food for the people in the cities, and they will be preserved.
verses.36: And it shall be a warning for the rulers of the earth during those seven years of famine that will occur in the land of Egypt. In those years, the land will not be able to bear the burden of famine.
verses.37: And this pleased Pharaoh and all his servants.
verses.38: And Pharaoh said to his servants, “Surely, there must be someone who has the spirit of God in him.”
verses.39: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “After God informed you of all this, there is no one more wise and intelligent than you.”
verses.40: You will be on my throne, and all nations will kiss your face. But the altar will be higher than you.
verses.41: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Look, I have appointed you over all the land of Egypt.”
verses.42: And Pharaoh took his crown off his head and handed it to Joseph. Then he wrapped the crown in seven layers of cloth, and he put gold around his neck.
verses.43: And he put it on the chariot that belonged to him. They called out to him, “Bless me!” and he placed it in all the lands of Egypt.
verses.44: And Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh. No one shall lay their hand or foot in all the land of Egypt.”
verses.45: And Pharaoh called out the name of Joseph, “Zaphnat Paneh.” He gave him Asenat, the daughter of Poti, as a wife for him. Then Joseph went away from Egypt.
verses.46: And Joseph, who was thirty years old, stood before Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. Joseph went out from before Pharaoh and traveled throughout all of Egypt’s land.
verses.47: And the earth was divided into seven parts, for the creation of the heavens.
verses.48: And he took in all the food that was available during those seven years when they were in Egypt. He also gave food to the townspeople, as well as to those who lived in the villages surrounding them.
verses.49: And Joseph kept counting the waves of the sea, until he stopped counting, for there were too many waves to count.
verses.50: And Joseph had two sons before the year of famine came. His wife, Asenath, gave birth to a son named Potipheh. Potipheh was a priest.
verses.51: And Joseph called out the name of the tomb, “Menashe.” For God has taken away all my toils and all the troubles of my father’s house.
verses.52: And the name of the second one was Ephraim, because God had redeemed the land from its poverty.
verses.53: And we counted seven and a half weeks that were in the land of Egypt.
verses.54: And we began to suffer seven years of famine, as Joseph said. There was a famine in all the lands. In every corner of Egypt, there was nothing but bread to eat.
verses.55: And the entire land of Egypt became barren due to hunger. The people cried out to Pharaoh for help. Pharaoh said to all the people of Egypt, “Go to Joseph, who will tell you what to do.”
verses.56: And famine spread over all the land. Joseph opened up all those who were in it, and he weakened the famine in Egypt’s land.
verses.57: And all the land came from Egypt to Joseph, because of the severe famine that affected the entire land.
